annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "Anna Livia" on page 199 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. In this Age of Gods (closing) passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
Mink, Louis O. A Finnegans Wake Gazetteer. https://archive.org/details/finneganswakegaz0000mink
FWEET: ALP / River Liffey concordance. https://www.fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "sleep" on page 199 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "hen" on page 199 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
